did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with the title “For the sons of Korah” and presents Jerusalem and its surroundings through the expression “the holy mountains.”
Did you know? According to the verse, the Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwelling places of Jacob, emphasizing Zion’s special choice.
Did you know? Jerusalem is called here “the city of God,” and glorious things—important and exalted things—are spoken about it.
Did you know? The psalm mentions various peoples and places together: Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush, presenting them in connection with their relationship to Zion.

Did you know? The phrase “This one was born there” is repeated in the psalm regarding the peoples mentioned. In the straightforward sense of the verse, Zion is portrayed as a place of birth or belonging even for people whose origins are in different lands.
Did you know? Of Zion it is said, “Everyone was born in her”—wording that emphasizes that each and every person may be regarded as one born there.
Did you know? The Lord is described as counting the nations and recording them in writing: “when He registers the peoples.” Within that record appears the declaration, “This one was born there.”
Did you know? At the end, singers and dancers join in expressing joy, saying, “All my springs are in you”—meaning that all their sources and longings are connected with Zion.
